title: Ireland–Claisen rearrangement
subtitle: An allyl ester becomes a silyl ketene acetal, which rearranges at room temperature
conditionsLabel: 1. LDA, THF, −78 °C · 2. Me₃SiCl · 3. warm to room temperature · 4. H₃O⁺ work-up

ester.caption: allyl propanoate and LDA in THF at −78 °C
ester.learnerPrompt: LDA is added to the ester at −78 °C. Draw the first step.
hintTiers: LDA is a strong, hindered base. Which hydrogen of the ester is the most acidic?
The hydrogen on the carbon next to the C=O (the α-carbon of the propanoyl group) is removed; its pair makes a C=C and the C=O pair moves onto oxygen. Three arrows: an ester enolate.
Arrow 1: from the nitrogen lone pair to the α-hydrogen. Arrow 2: from the α C–H bond to the bond between the α-carbon and the carbonyl carbon. Arrow 3: from the C=O π bond onto the carbonyl oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: LDA is far too hindered to add to the C=O: its two isopropyl groups keep the nitrogen away from carbon. It only takes protons.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Two of three: the carbonyl carbon would now have five bonds. Move the C=O π pair onto oxygen.

enolate.caption: the lithium ester enolate and diisopropylamine

enolate-and-chlorotrimethylsilane.caption: the enolate with chlorotrimethylsilane
enolate-and-chlorotrimethylsilane.learnerPrompt: Chlorotrimethylsilane traps the enolate. Draw how the enolate attacks silicon.
hintTiers: An enolate can react through carbon or through oxygen. Silicon forms a very strong bond to one of them.
The negatively charged oxygen attacks silicon and chloride leaves: an SN2-like substitution at silicon. Two arrows.
Arrow 1: from a lone pair on the enolate oxygen to a new bond with silicon. Arrow 2: from the Si–Cl bond onto chlorine.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Most electrophiles do attack an enolate through carbon, but silicon is different: the Si–O bond is one of the strongest single bonds there is, so silicon goes onto oxygen and makes a silyl ketene acetal.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: oxygen bonds to silicon. Silicon already has four bonds, so one must break: let chloride leave with the Si–Cl pair.

silyl-ketene-acetal.caption: the silyl ketene acetal, drawn curled so its ends meet
silyl-ketene-acetal.learnerPrompt: On warming to room temperature the silyl ketene acetal rearranges. Draw the single step.
hintTiers: Look for a 1,5-diene with an oxygen in it: C=C, then oxygen, then the allyl group. Six atoms, six electrons, one step.
The O–CH₂ bond to the allyl group breaks, the α-carbon bonds to the far CH₂ of the allyl group, and the ester oxygen gets a C=O again. Three arrows.

Arrow 1: from the ketene acetal C=C π bond to a new bond between the α-carbon and the far CH₂ of the allyl group. Arrow 2: from the O–allyl σ bond to the bond between that oxygen and the central carbon (it becomes C=O). Arrow 3: from the allyl C=C π bond to the bond between its CH and the CH₂ that lost oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Breaking the O–allyl bond on its own would give a carboxylate and an allyl cation. In a Claisen rearrangement this bond breaks only as the new C–C bond forms, in one cyclic step with no ions.
The trimethylsilyl group stays on its oxygen until work-up. The bond that breaks is the one between the other oxygen and the allyl CH₂.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the O–allyl bond becomes a C=O π bond. In the same step the ketene acetal C=C reaches the far end of the allyl group and the allyl π bond moves across. Two more arrows.

silyl-ester.caption: trimethylsilyl 2-methylpent-4-enoate; aqueous acid then gives 2-methylpent-4-enoic acid

steps.explanationAfterStep: An ester α-hydrogen has pKa about 25 and diisopropylamine about 36, so LDA turns all the ester into its lithium enolate at −78 °C, before anything else can happen. In THF the enolate forms mainly with the methyl group trans to the oxygen bearing lithium (Ireland's (E)-enolate); adding HMPA reverses this. The app does not check stereochemistry yet, so the drawings carry no wedges and no E/Z marks.
Silicon is attacked through oxygen, giving a silyl ketene acetal: a neutral, isolable enol ether of the ester. It is also an allyl vinyl ether, so it is set up for a Claisen rearrangement.

A [3,3]-sigmatropic shift, the Claisen rearrangement of an allyl vinyl ether. The electron-rich ketene acetal makes it fast: it runs at room temperature, where an ordinary allyl vinyl ether needs about 180 °C. The product is a silyl ester; aqueous acid at work-up cleaves the O–Si bond to give 2-methylpent-4-enoic acid. The chair transition state turns the enolate geometry into the relative configuration of the new stereocentres when the allyl group is substituted. The app does not check stereochemistry yet, so the drawings carry no wedges and no E/Z marks.

mechanismSummary: The Ireland–Claisen rearrangement makes a γ,δ-unsaturated carboxylic acid from an allyl ester. LDA forms the ester enolate, chlorotrimethylsilane traps it on oxygen as a silyl ketene acetal, and this allyl vinyl ether undergoes a [3,3]-sigmatropic shift through a chair-like transition state at room temperature. Work-up hydrolyses the silyl ester to the acid (not drawn). Because the enolate geometry can be controlled (THF or THF/HMPA), and the chair transition state passes it on, the relative stereochemistry of the product is predictable. The app does not check stereochemistry yet, so the drawings carry no wedges and no E/Z marks.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 35
